methodValidationCard.title: Canary Execution
methodValidationCard.detail: Execution framework is live and accumulating proof data. Promotion to live trading is gated on measured outcomes.

transparencyUpdates.title: Canary execution framework live — dry-run phase started
transparencyUpdates.summary: The automated execution framework is now running in dry-run mode. Promotion to live trading is gated on a measured proof window, not on operator discretion.
bullets: Execution decisions are fully automated: each trade candidate is evaluated against safety constraints, capital lane rules, and a time-windowed proof requirement before anything is allowed.
A signing policy enforcement gate now sits in the execution path. Hardware wallet confirmation is required above a notional threshold. Every decision — allow or deny — is recorded in an audit log.
The proof window requires positive measured outcomes across both a short and medium horizon before the system can promote itself from dry-run to live. No manual override path exists.

Wallet inventory and exchange balances are read-only inputs to the system. Credentials are resolved exclusively from the OS keychain at runtime — no plaintext secrets anywhere in the codebase or config.
nextSteps: Accumulate dry-run execution data over the coming weeks.
Monitor proof window status in the operator cockpit.
Promote to live only after the measured proof window clears its gate.

transparencyUpdates.title: Platform quality foundation complete — all gates met
transparencyUpdates.summary: A suite of binding quality gates was defined and then met before any further feature work proceeded. This was a deliberate discipline step, not a byproduct of regular development.
bullets: Backend and frontend test coverage both exceed the 80% line threshold. Frontend branch and function coverage also clear their respective gates. These are enforced in CI — a drop below the gate blocks the build.
The operator cockpit was decomposed from a single large file into focused, single-responsibility modules. The main route is now under 200 lines — pure wiring with no logic embedded.
All JavaScript files in the tooling layer were converted to TypeScript. Type safety now extends to every script in the repository, not just the application code.
A doc link checker runs in CI and rejects broken internal documentation links. 25 pre-existing broken links were fixed as part of this work.
nextSteps: Maintain coverage gates on every future change — CI enforces this automatically.
Keep the cockpit route under the 200-line gate as new operator surfaces are added.
Let proof data from the running canary guide the next round of platform improvements.

transparencyUpdates.title: DeFi research lane opened with explicit risk scoring
transparencyUpdates.summary: A structured DeFi opportunity research layer is now part of the platform. It scores and surfaces opportunities alongside explicit risk fields that most DeFi UIs hide or understate.
bullets: Every DeFi opportunity surfaced by the platform now carries three explicit risk dimensions: impermanent loss exposure, smart contract risk score, and governance risk level. These are first-class fields, not footnotes.

The research lane is read-only and informational. No DeFi execution path exists. This is intentional: the gate for DeFi execution requires DeFi to demonstrably beat the best CEX path on after-tax, after-fee compounding — a bar it has not yet cleared.
Gross APY figures are displayed alongside a net-of-fees, net-of-risk estimate so the operator sees realistic take-home returns rather than headline numbers.
The research lane is documented for DeFi-literate readers with a full explanation of why each risk dimension matters and what drives the scores.
nextSteps: Expand the opportunity catalogue as more protocol data becomes available.
Continue accumulating CEX proof data to establish the baseline that DeFi must beat.
Publish further research notes on IL, governance risk, and smart contract failure modes.

transparencyUpdates.title: Walk-forward out-of-sample validation added to strategy research
transparencyUpdates.summary: Strategy research results now include mandatory out-of-sample validation across multiple time windows. In-sample performance alone is no longer sufficient to advance a candidate.
bullets: Each strategy research run now produces walk-forward validation windows: the dataset is split into training and holdout periods across multiple cut points, and performance is measured on data the strategy never saw during fitting.

A robustness summary across all windows classifies each candidate as promote-ready, watch-only, or no robust candidate available. This classification, not in-sample metrics, drives the promotion decision.
The walk-forward computation is deterministic: two independent runs on the same data produce identical windows and identical robustness classifications. This is tested in CI.

Blocker-targeted experiment records now capture the specific hypothesis tested, the measured result, and the decision reached — creating an auditable research trail rather than a list of ad-hoc backtests.
nextSteps: Feed live execution data into the research pipeline as the canary accumulates outcomes.
Use walk-forward robustness status to guide which strategy candidates enter dry-run.
Expand the experiment record schema to cover more candidate families as research broadens.
